t:
(a) Ground Ambulance.—Section 1834(l)(13)(A) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395m(l)(13)(A)) is amended—
        (1) in the matter preceding clause (i), by striking “January 1, 2014” and inserting “April 1, 2014”; and 
        (2) in each of clauses (i) and (ii), by striking “January 1, 2014” and inserting “April 1, 2014” each place it appears.  
    (b) Super Rural Ground Ambulance.—Section 1834(l)(12)(A) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395m(l)(12)(A)) is amended by striking “January 1, 2014” and inserting “April 1, 2014”.

fable.w: This section only extends the dates for Medicare ground ambulance add-on payments by amending date references in the Social Security Act. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, hearing, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

opus.w: The section only extends the deadline for ground ambulance and super rural ground ambulance payment provisions from January 1, 2014 to April 1, 2014. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision, and no rulemaking or comment process is required. Affecting outside parties such as ambulance providers is not the same as having them participate.

qwen_chat.w: The section solely amends specific dates in the Social Security Act regarding ground ambulance reimbursement. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are direct legislative mandates without any procedural requirement for external participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing dates for ambulance reimbursement rules implies a regulatory process that could involve public comment. However, the text itself only specifies date changes to existing statutory provisions and does not mention any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body. It is a direct legislative amendment, not a procedural requirement for participation.
